cells.tense: The fairness is running at the table right now, and you are the one holding the pen.
cells.ask: Pick one recurring moment this week and write down what you actually did, no verdict. Let the notes show you the shape of your own fairness.
cells.core:
You can feel who is giving and who is taking before anyone speaks. Not the words — the pattern underneath, the shift in a room you can name only after it's moved. That reading is yours, and it's accurate, and it doesn't cost you your footing. You stay in the moment while you see it.

What comes next for this is release: letting a thing end when it has ended, trusting the new thing to arrive. You've earned the right to say how a thing should go, and the question now is what you hand back to the ground once you've read it. Notes, not verdicts, is the whole ask.

cells.tense: You're already judging how the next conversation will land, before it has started.
cells.ask: Take one exchange you're predicting and let it happen without your verdict. Say what you felt after, not what you planned. Forty words, written down.
cells.core:
The bookkeeping is running ahead of the room. You're working out what's fair before anyone has spoken, rehearsing the call, bracing for the moment you'll have to rule. The math gets more precise the less it's needed, and the flow it was meant to protect starts to feel like a case you're building.

The pattern you're reading is real — that part is not the problem. The problem is you're solving a version of the room that hasn't happened yet, so the actual people in front of you keep arriving after the verdict. Holding without forcing: strength that contains rather than crushes. Let the exchange come first and the fairness follow.

cells.tense: There was a door you stopped at, and you're still standing behind it.
cells.ask: For one week, when a room's fairness is off, write three lines of what you noticed. Just the observation, kept in a notebook nobody reads.
cells.core:
You notice who is getting less, whose temperature just dropped, and it doesn't make it out of you. So you carry the reading alone and the room carries on without it. The offering stopped; the noticing didn't.

What's starved isn't fairness. It's the machinery of going in with fresh eyes and finding out whether the pattern holds. Practice flows without force — solitude that connects, refinement that isn't fear. Feed that side and the reading comes back through. Pushing feeling at the quiet spot doesn't work; leave it alone and build the other one.

cells.tense: You're already making the calls about what's fair here, and you're reporting them as luck or circumstance.
cells.ask: Name one judgment you made about what was fair here and say, out loud to one person, 'I decided that.' Your call, nothing more.
cells.core:
The authority is running. Somebody is making the calls about what's fair in the rooms you're in — who gets heard, what gets weighed, when the temperature shifts — and that somebody is you. It gets told as the situation, the obvious thing, the way it works, because that story is easier to carry than the claim.

The reading stays accurate either way. What's missing is the acknowledgment: this is your judgment, made by you, answerable to you. The simpler form of the same line is just listening — fresh ears, no verdict yet — because a call you can't name is a call you can't correct. Say it once and the pattern gets a witness.
